newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt's Haikal stands in respect for Tel Aviv bomber.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's Haikal stands in respect for Tel Aviv bomber.

text.p: Prominent Egyptian writer and commentator Mohamed Hassanein Haikal said he "stands up in respect" for the Palestinian suicide bomber who killed three Israeli women in a Tel Aviv cafe last week.

Haikal, a close confidant of late Egyptian president Gamal Abdel Nasser and a prolific author on Middle East politics, said in an interview published on Monday the man had sacrificed himself for an objective out of desperation.
"I may not agree with what he did, but..I cannot but stand up in respect at his sacrificing himself for an objective," he told the independent Egyptian newspaper al-Osboa.
"If anyone describes this act as pointless or mad, let me tell them that they are wrong... I cannot judge him on the basis that what he committed was a crime.
"He was driven to despair... I think he made a misjudgment but he did a human act in which he gave his life for a goal he believed in -- wrong or right is another matter," he added.
He was answering a question on both the Palestinian suicide bomber and the Jordanian soldier who killed seven Israeli schoolgirls on the Israeli-Jordanian border this month.
Haikal said Egyptians could not say they were resisting the policies of the Israeli government while at the same normal relations continued between the two states.
"This is where talk loses credibility. We really need to take a look at ourselves and reconsider everything," he added.
